evidence: Recorded BMI equals round(weight / (height/100)^2, 1) for 6,388 of 6,388 cases, so it is computed from the recorded height and weight and carries no information of its own about the true values.
api: Return the distribution of weight/(height/100)^2 with height and weight drawn from their own posteriors for the same case; optionally include measurement variability. The recorded BMI is used only as a consistency check.
limitations: Height and weight posteriors are drawn independently given sex and age; their correlation is ignored. This matters only when an input posterior is wide (written-in values).
